content.value_statement: Software documentation often becomes fragmented across formats and project stages. This skill provides a phased workflow for planning, creating, publishing, and maintaining it.
actual_capabilities: Organizes documentation work into eight phases from planning through maintenance.
Directs API reference and OpenAPI specification workflows.
Coordinates C4 and Mermaid architecture documentation.
Covers code comments, function references, and usage examples.
Plans README files, tutorials, wikis, and onboarding guides.
Defines release documentation tasks and six documentation quality gates.
limitations: Requires separately available named skills for specialized generation tasks.
Provides workflow guidance but includes no scripts, templates, or publishing configuration.
Generated documentation still requires technical review and environment-specific validation.
Does not verify links, examples, APIs, or diagrams automatically.

use_cases.title: Document a new service
use_cases.description: Plan a README, API reference, setup guide, and examples for a software service.

use_cases.title: Describe system architecture
use_cases.description: Coordinate context, container, component, sequence, data flow, and deployment documentation.

use_cases.title: Maintain a documentation portal
use_cases.description: Structure wiki pages, onboarding guides, release notes, references, and recurring quality reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Outline project documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation plan for [project], including its audience, README sections, setup guide, usage examples, and review checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new project

prompt_templates.title: Plan an API reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan API documentation for [service] from [source], covering endpoints, schemas, authentication, examples, OpenAPI output, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Design architecture documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a C4 documentation set for [system], including context, containers, components, data flows, sequences, deployment, and Mermaid diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate the full workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased documentation program for [product], assigning deliverables, specialist skills, dependencies, quality gates, owners, and maintenance intervals.

output_examples.input: Plan documentation for a new payment API used by external developers.
output: Planning: define audiences, terminology, ownership, and publication structure.
API reference: document authentication, endpoints, schemas, errors, and complete requests.
Guides: add setup, first transaction, testing, troubleshooting, and migration topics.
Quality gates: validate examples, links, API coverage, and release ownership.

output_examples.input: Create an architecture documentation plan for a distributed order system.
output: Start with system context and external dependencies.
Describe services, data stores, queues, and deployment boundaries.
Add component, sequence, data flow, and failure recovery views.
Review diagrams whenever interfaces or deployment topology change.

output_examples.input: Improve an outdated internal engineering wiki.
output_examples.output: The plan inventories pages, assigns owners, restructures navigation, updates onboarding content, repairs links, and schedules recurring reviews.

best_practices: Define audiences, scope, owners, and quality criteria before generating content.
Validate every example, link, diagram, and API statement against the current system.
Update documentation with code, interface, deployment, and release changes.
anti_patterns: Do not invoke every listed specialist skill when the task needs only one document.
Do not publish generated technical claims without review by a responsible subject expert.
Do not create duplicate references when an authoritative source already exists.

faq.question: Does this skill generate documentation directly?
faq.answer: It primarily coordinates a workflow and recommends specialized skills. Actual generation depends on available tools and project context.

faq.question: Which documentation types are covered?
faq.answer: It covers API, architecture, code, README, tutorial, wiki, onboarding, changelog, release, reference, and process documentation.

faq.question: Can it create OpenAPI specifications?
faq.answer: It includes an OpenAPI phase and directs an OpenAPI specialist, but the specialist must be installed and given accurate API sources.

faq.question: Does it support architecture diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow covers C4, Mermaid, sequence, data flow, component, and deployment diagrams through named specialist skills.

faq.question: Can it validate generated documentation?
faq.answer: It supplies quality gates, but it does not automatically test examples, check links, or verify technical accuracy.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best results?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, source files, system boundaries, publishing target, style rules, owners, and required deliverables.
